page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The arm64 architecture offers a distinct resource density profile, providing a cost-efficient option for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores with a lower memory footprint. Due to the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is designed for compute-heavy tasks such as web serving, containerized microservices, and distributed build systems that do not require massive memory allocations or local NVMe storage.
